Let $f:W\to Z$ be a filtered L∞-morphism as in [[def-filtered-l-infinity-morphism]], and put $P=F^1W$, $P'=F^1Z$. On $C(P)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S^nP$, including $S^0P=k\cdot1$, use the symmetric multiplication and the counital coproduct

$$\Delta(x_1\cdots x_n)=\sum_{I\sqcup J=\{1,\ldots,n\}}\epsilon(I,J;x)x_I\otimes x_J.$$

Empty subsets are allowed. Define $\mathcal F^NC(P)$ as the span of products $x_1\cdots x_n$ with $x_j\in F^{i_j}W$, all $i_j\ge1$, and $\sum_j i_j\ge N$; scalars have weight zero. Define the **completed coaugmented symmetric coalgebra**

$$\widehat C(P)=\varprojlim_N C(P)/\mathcal F^NC(P).$$

All completions and limits are degreewise. Complete tensor products for coproducts with the sum of the two weight filtrations. Then multiplication, coproduct, counit and coaugmentation extend continuously, as do $Q$ and the Taylor map $F$. Their continuous extensions satisfy $Q^2=0$, $\Delta F=(F\widehat\otimes F)\Delta$, and $FQ=RF$. The length-one projection extends continuously to $p_P:\widehat C(P)\to P$.

For $w\in P^0$ and homogeneous $v\in F^pW$, $p\ge1$, define the convergent expressions

$$e^w=\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{w^n}{n!},\qquad c_q(w)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{q_n(w^n)}{n!},\qquad u=f_*(w)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{f_n(w^n)}{n!}.$$

They satisfy

$$\Delta e^w=e^w\otimes e^w,\qquad e^we^{-w}=1,\qquad Q(e^w)=c_q(w)e^w,\qquad F(e^w)=e^u,$$

and the marked-input identity

$$F(ve^w)=\left(\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{f_{n+1}(w^n,v)}{n!}\right)e^u.$$

This is a total filtration weight completion on the positive ideal, not an unspecified product by symmetric arity on all of $W$.

For a complete filtered L∞-algebra in the convention of
[[def-complete-filtered-l-infinity-algebra]], a **Maurer–Cartan element** is
an element $w\in F^1W^0$ satisfying

$$\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{1}{n!}q_n(w,\ldots,w)=0.$$

The series is the unique limit proved in
[[thm-filtered-l-infinity-maurer-cartan-series-converges]]. This equation
defines a set of solutions; it does not by itself specify a deformation
problem or an equivalence relation on those solutions.

Let $W$ be a complete filtered shifted L∞-algebra over a characteristic-zero field $k$. Put $P=F^1W$ with its induced filtration. This is a complete closed subspace: it is the kernel of $W\to W/F^1W$, and compatible cosets in $P/F^pW$ have their unique $W$-limit in that kernel. All $q_n$ preserve $P$.

The **completed polynomial coefficients** and **completed polynomial differential forms** mean

$$P[t]^{\wedge}=\varprojlim_p (P/F^pW)\otimes_k k[t],\qquad P\widehat\otimes\Omega=\varprojlim_p (P/F^pW)\otimes_k k[t,dt],\quad |t|=0,\quad |dt|=1.$$

These are compatible polynomials in each quotient; their degrees need not have a common bound. Evaluation at $0,1$, differentiation, and integration from $0$ to $t$ are defined in every quotient by polynomial formulas and commute with reduction; integration uses $\int_0^t u^jdu=t^{j+1}/(j+1)$. Operations on these spaces are extended continuously, with each coefficient of a fixed quotient a finite sum.

Write $C(w)=\sum_{n\ge1}q_n(w^n)/n!$ and $q_1^w(a)=\sum_{n\ge0}q_{n+1}(w^n,a)/n!$. An **elementary gauge path** is a pair $w\in P^0[t]^{\wedge}$, $a\in P^{-1}[t]^{\wedge}$ such that $C(w)=0$ and $w'=q_1^w(a)$. Its endpoints are $w(0),w(1)$. **Gauge equivalence** is the equivalence relation generated by endpoints of these paths. A constant path has $a=0$; reversal is $(w(1-t),-a(1-t))$; finite chains give transitivity. Polynomial concatenation is not required.

For the polynomial-form interpretation, forms are placed on the right. For homogeneous $x_i\in P$, $\alpha_i\in\Omega$, the extension of $q_n$ has scalar sign $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}|\alpha_i||x_j|}$; its unary part also contains $(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes d\alpha$. The degree-zero form $z=w-a\,dt$ then satisfies $C_{\Omega}(z)=C(w)+(w'-q_1^w(a))dt$. Thus these paths are precisely Maurer–Cartan elements over the completed polynomial interval. This fixes a gauge construction using the full operations, rather than choosing an arbitrary equivalence relation on a solution set.

Let $f:W\to Z$ be a filtered L∞-morphism as in [[def-filtered-l-infinity-morphism]], and put $P=F^1W$, $P'=F^1Z$. On $C(P)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S^nP$, including $S^0P=k\cdot1$, use the symmetric multiplication and the counital coproduct

$$\Delta(x_1\cdots x_n)=\sum_{I\sqcup J=\{1,\ldots,n\}}\epsilon(I,J;x)x_I\otimes x_J.$$

Empty subsets are allowed. Define $\mathcal F^NC(P)$ as the span of products $x_1\cdots x_n$ with $x_j\in F^{i_j}W$, all $i_j\ge1$, and $\sum_j i_j\ge N$; scalars have weight zero. Define the **completed coaugmented symmetric coalgebra**

$$\widehat C(P)=\varprojlim_N C(P)/\mathcal F^NC(P).$$

All completions and limits are degreewise. Complete tensor products for coproducts with the sum of the two weight filtrations. Then multiplication, coproduct, counit and coaugmentation extend continuously, as do $Q$ and the Taylor map $F$. Their continuous extensions satisfy $Q^2=0$, $\Delta F=(F\widehat\otimes F)\Delta$, and $FQ=RF$. The length-one projection extends continuously to $p_P:\widehat C(P)\to P$.

For $w\in P^0$ and homogeneous $v\in F^pW$, $p\ge1$, define the convergent expressions

$$e^w=\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{w^n}{n!},\qquad c_q(w)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{q_n(w^n)}{n!},\qquad u=f_*(w)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{f_n(w^n)}{n!}.$$

They satisfy

$$\Delta e^w=e^w\otimes e^w,\qquad e^we^{-w}=1,\qquad Q(e^w)=c_q(w)e^w,\qquad F(e^w)=e^u,$$

and the marked-input identity

$$F(ve^w)=\left(\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{f_{n+1}(w^n,v)}{n!}\right)e^u.$$

derivations.claim: For any dg scalar algebra $A$ put $P\widehat\otimes A=\varprojlim_N((P/F^NW)\otimes A)$, with filtration the kernels of the projections. Each projection is surjective: lift the finitely many coefficients of any algebraic tensor to $P$, giving a compatible element of the inverse limit. The quotient by its kernel is therefore exactly the displayed algebraic tensor product. The limit is complete and separated, degreewise. Tensoring over the field preserves exact sequences, so each graded filtration layer is its corresponding algebraic tensor product with $A$. Here every input lies in $P$, so the additive filtration bounds also show independence of the chosen representatives modulo $F^NW$. The operations in the statement are well defined on every quotient, and the input filtration indices add under each operation; they thus extend continuously to the limit.

To verify the signs and identities on algebraic tensors, move each scalar $a_i$ past every later $W$ factor $x_j$, then apply the $W$ operation and multiply the scalars in their original order. This gives precisely the exponent $\sum_{i<j}|a_i||x_j|$. This movement respects substitution: the product of its signs in two substituted operations is the sign of the composite permutation, including the sign of moving a degree-one inner operation across earlier inputs. Consequently the part of each shifted Jacobi identity involving only the extended $q_n$ is the original $W$ identity multiplied by the common ordered scalar product. Its sum is zero. Write $D(x\otimes a)=(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes d_Aa$ for the scalar differential. For an extended operation of degree $d$, let $E=\sum_{i<j}|a_i||x_j|$. The coefficient of the scalar product with $d_Aa_i$ in the output differential has sign exponent $E+\sum_j|x_j|+d+\sum_{j<i}|a_j|$. The same coefficient obtained by applying the tensor differential to the $i$th input first has exponent $E+\sum_j|x_j|+\sum_{j<i}|a_j|$: the extra scalar crossing signs are $\sum_{j>i}|x_j|$, and the tensor differential contributes $\sum_{j<i}(|x_j|+|a_j|)+|x_i|$. Thus the two expressions differ by $(-1)^d$. For $d=1$ this proves that $D$ anticommutes with each extended $q_n$. Also $D^2=0$. Thus the full coderivation with unary term $q_1^A$ squares to zero. This checks the scalar-differential terms as well as the original Jacobi terms.

The same permutation and substitution verification transfers $FQ=RF$ to scalar tensors. Here each $f_n$ has degree zero, so the scalar differential commutes with $f_n$; its Leibniz expansion supplies precisely all the terms in which a scalar differential appears on an input. Thus the stated $f_n^A$ form a filtered morphism. These are finite identities on each algebraic tensor and each fixed arity. They descend to every quotient and hold on the inverse limit by continuity. Any dg algebra map $\rho:A\to B$ preserves scalar products, scalar differentials and degrees, so $\operatorname{id}\widehat\otimes\rho$ commutes with all these operations. Applying [F1] to the extended algebras proves their curvature and composition identities; in particular $\rho_*(f_*^A(z))=f_*^B(\rho_*(z))$.

For $A=\Omega$, every total-degree-zero element in the positive ideal has a unique expression $z=w(t)-a(t)dt$ with the degrees in the statement. All these functions are polynomials at each quotient and their degrees may grow with $N$. Differentiation, multiplication and evaluation at any $\lambda\in k$ are defined quotientwise and respect the transition maps. The scalar differential of $w$ contributes $w'(t)dt$. The input $-a(t)dt$ appearing once in $q_{n+1}^\Omega$ contributes $-q_{n+1}(w(t)^n,a(t))dt$: place this input last, so it crosses no later $W$ factor. Because $w$ and $-a dt$ both have total degree zero, its $n+1$ possible positions contribute equally, changing $1/(n+1)!$ to $1/n!$. Applying the identical one-marked-input computation to $f_*^\Omega$ gives $f_*^\Omega(z)=u(t)-b(t)dt$, where $u=f_*w$ and $b=\sum_{n\ge0}f_{n+1}(w^n,a)/n!$. Each summand of the latter series lies in filtration $n+1$; the corresponding statement for $u$ is [F1]. Thus only finitely many terms survive in each quotient, and these terms are polynomials. By curvature transformation over $\Omega$ from step 3.1, $z$ Maurer–Cartan implies $u-bdt$ Maurer–Cartan. The curvature decomposition of step 3.2 applied on $Z$ now proves $c_r(u)=0$ and $u'=r_1^u(b)$.

Evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_\lambda:\Omega\to k$, $t\mapsto\lambda$, $dt\mapsto0$, is a dg algebra map. Naturality in step 3.1 yields $\operatorname{ev}_\lambda f_*^\Omega(z)=f_*(w(\lambda))$. In particular the endpoint values are precisely those in the statement. If the input path is specified as the unique flow supplied by [F3], it satisfies the equations in step 3.2; its image satisfies the corresponding target flow equations and is the target flow for $b$ and initial value $f_*(w(0))$ by [F3]. This proves the assertion for every such input parameter as well.

Every generating endpoint pair for the equivalence relation in [F2] maps, by the path and endpoint calculations, to another such pair. Finite chains of generating pairs and their reverses therefore map to chains of the same kind; equality maps to equality. This proves preservation of the generated equivalence relation without claiming that a concatenation itself is polynomial. Composition and identities over $\Omega$ follow from step 3.1 and [F1]. derivations.claim: By [[lem-complete-coderivations-form-a-filtered-differential-graded-lie-algebra]], $\mathfrak g$ is a complete filtered differential graded Lie algebra. Since $D$ and $R$ have degree one and $D^2=0$, direct expansion gives $(D+R)^2=DR+RD+R^2=dR+[R,R]/2$. Thus the displayed assignment is an object bijection, with inverse subtraction of $D$.

By [[thm-coalgebra-automorphism-logarithms-are-coderivations]], every allowed $G$ has the unique form $G=\exp X$ with $X\in\mathfrak g^0$. The conjugation identity in [[lem-noncommutative-filtered-exponential-and-logarithm]] gives $G(D+R)G^{-1}=e^{\operatorname{ad}_X}(D+R)$. Since $[X,D]=-dX$, subtracting $D$ gives precisely the displayed action. Each term has increasing coefficient order. Conjugation preserves coderivations, their square-zero condition, and reduction to $D$, so this is an action on the object set. The group law is composition, transported through exp and log; no unproved BCH construction is needed.

Let $s:\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak g[1]$ have degree $-1$. The shift lemma in the statement has $q_1(sx)=-s(dx)$ and $q_2(sx,sy)=(-1)^{|x|}s[x,y]$, with no higher operations. Hence the shifted curvature at $sR$ is $-s(dR+[R,R]/2)$, and its gauge vector with parameter $s\xi$ is $s(-d\xi+[\xi,R])$. Therefore the exact path equation of [[def-filtered-maurer-cartan-gauge-path]] is $R'=-d\xi+[\xi,R]$ for compatible polynomial coefficients $R(t)$ and $\xi(t)$, with $\xi(t)\in\mathfrak g^0[t]^{\wedge}=\varprojlim_n(\mathfrak g^0/F^n\mathfrak g^0)\otimes k[t]$. The scalar variable has degree zero, and algebraic integration divides $t^j$ by $j+1$ in the usual way.

Fix any such variable parameter $\xi(t)$ and write $E[t]^{\wedge}=\varprojlim_n(E/F^nE)\otimes k[t]$. Starting at $U_0=V_0=\operatorname{id}$, iterate $U_{a+1}(t)=\operatorname{id}+\int_0^t\xi(u)U_a(u)\,du$ and $V_{a+1}(t)=\operatorname{id}-\int_0^tV_a(u)\xi(u)\,du$. Multiplication by $\xi$ raises coefficient order by one, so successive differences have order at least $a+1$. Every quotient consequently stabilizes after finitely many iterations as a polynomial. Completeness gives unique solutions $U'=\xi U$, $V'=-V\xi$, $U(0)=V(0)=\operatorname{id}$. Uniqueness follows from the same integral equation: a difference in $F^a$ must lie in $F^{a+1}$, and the filtration is separated.

Differentiating gives $(VU)'=-V\xi U+V\xi U=0$, and its initial value is the identity, so $VU=\operatorname{id}$. Similarly $Z=UV-\operatorname{id}$ satisfies $Z'=\xi Z-Z\xi$ and $Z(0)=0$. Its integral equation raises coefficient order and forces $Z$ into every $F^a$, so $UV=\operatorname{id}$. Thus $V=U^{-1}$ as completed polynomial endomorphisms.

In the completed tensor target put $H=\Delta U-(U\otimes U)\Delta$. The coderivation equation for $\xi$ and the product rule give $H'=(\xi\otimes1+1\otimes\xi)H$ and $H(0)=0$. Its integral equation forces successive coefficient orders and hence $H=0$. The same argument applied to $U(1_C)-1_C$ gives zero, using $\xi(1_C)=0$; and $(\epsilon U)'=\epsilon\xi U=0$ gives $\epsilon U=\epsilon$. Together with step 3.1 these prove that $U(t)$, and in particular $U(1)$, is an actual continuous coaugmented counital coalgebra automorphism congruent to the identity modulo $I$. All equations are quotientwise polynomial equations, not analytic-time claims.

For an initial deformation $K_0=D+R_0$, set $K(t)=U(t)K_0V(t)$. Differentiation gives $K'=[\xi,K]$, and $K(0)=K_0$. Consequently $R(t)=K(t)-D$ satisfies $R'=-d\xi+[\xi,R]$, and $K(t)^2=U K_0^2V=0$. Any other completed polynomial solution with the same parameter and initial value differs by $Z'= [\xi,Z]$, $Z(0)=0$, whose integral equation raises order and forces $Z=0$. Every elementary shifted gauge path is therefore this actual conjugation path for its own parameter and initial value. Its endpoints are conjugate by the allowed automorphism $U(1)$, and any finite chain of such paths remains conjugate by composition.

Conversely suppose an allowed $G$ carries $D+R_0$ to $D+R_1$. Step 2.1 gives $X=\log G\in\mathfrak g^0$. Set $U(t)=\exp(tX)$; its series is polynomial modulo each coefficient order, and step 2.1's coalgebra exponential theorem applies coefficientwise in $t$. The path $U(t)(D+R_0)U(t)^{-1}-D$ has parameter $\xi(t)=X$, is Maurer–Cartan for every $t$, and joins $R_0$ to $R_1$. Step 2.2 identifies it as an elementary shifted gauge path. Thus every allowed equivalence lies in the gauge relation.

Step 5.1 proves gauge-equivalent elements give equivalent deformations, and step 6.1 proves the converse. Combining this equivalence of relations with the object bijection in step 1.1 proves the claimed bijection on quotient classes, with the full equivalence group and displayed action of step 2.1.

For the tensor carrier, [F7] identifies every positive-arity Taylor family with the native unsuspended A∞ operations by the invertible suspension maps and fixed signs, and identifies every intertwining coalgebra map with exactly its native A∞ morphism. Its finite-word identities hold over each coefficient quotient $B/I^n$ because tensoring the displayed coefficient identities preserves their equalities; the insertion and primitive uniqueness arguments use no division in the tensor case. Passing to the separated coefficient limit gives all continuous completed operations and maps. Reduction to the fixed structure and to the identity is unchanged by these invertible signs. For the symmetric carrier, [F8] is exactly the degree-one coderivation definition; adjoining the coaugmentation and extending a coderivation by zero on it preserves its equation. Its finite unshuffle formulas extend through the coefficient quotients, with all integer denominators invertible over the characteristic-zero base. Thus the objects and full equivalences in step 7.1 are precisely the two asserted fixed-carrier homotopy-algebra deformation problems in their stated conventions.

citations.quote:
Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, let $B$ be a commutative unital $k$-algebra concentrated in degree zero, and let $I$ be an ideal such that $B\cong\varprojlim_{n\ge1}B/I^n$. Nilpotent ideals are included. Let $V$ be any graded $k$-vector space; no finite-dimensionality assumption is made. Use the graded tensor convention of [[def-koszul-sign-rule-for-graded-tensors]].

The carrier $C$ is either the coaugmented tensor coalgebra $T^c(V)=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}V^{\otimes r}$ with deconcatenation, or the coaugmented graded symmetric coalgebra $S^c(V)=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}S^r(V)$ with unshuffle coproduct. For the latter, $S^r$ means graded symmetric coinvariants, and the coproduct sums over all divisions of the inputs into two ordered sublists, with the Koszul sign. The empty word is $1_C$, the counit $\epsilon$ is projection to length zero, and the coaugmentation is inclusion of scalars. These formulas specify the carrier without requiring a cofree universal property.

Define its coefficient completion, filtration, and tensor target by

$$C_B=\varprojlim_n(C\otimes_k B/I^n),\qquad F^nC_B=\ker(C_B\longrightarrow C\otimes_k B/I^n),\qquad F^0C_B=C_B.$$

$$C_B\widehat\otimes_B C_B=\varprojlim_n((C\otimes_k C)\otimes_k B/I^n).$$

All structure maps are extended through these inverse limits. This is coefficient completion of a direct sum: modulo each $I^n$ every element has finite length support. No unrestricted product over arities is included. Completed tensor powers and polynomial coefficients mean the analogous explicit inverse limits. A homogeneous map is understood in the grading induced by $C$, and continuity always means the displayed coefficient topology.

Let $E$ be the graded composition algebra of continuous $B$-linear filtration-preserving endomorphisms of $C_B$. Its order filtration is

$$F^pE=\{T:T(F^qC_B)\subseteq F^{p+q}C_B\text{ for every }q\ge0\}\quad(p\ge0).$$

Let $\mathfrak l\subset E$ be the homogeneous coderivations satisfying $T(1_C)=0$, $\epsilon T=0$, and

$$\Delta T=(T\otimes1+1\otimes T)\Delta.$$

The sign in $1\otimes T$ is the graded tensor sign. In particular these coderivations have zero nullary component. Fix $D\in\mathfrak l^1$ with $D^2=0$. A **coefficient-complete fixed-carrier codifferential deformation** is $D+R$ with $R\in F^1\mathfrak l^1$ and $(D+R)^2=0$. Its allowed equivalences are degree-zero continuous $B$-linear counital coaugmented coalgebra automorphisms $G$ such that $G-\operatorname{id}\in F^1E$, acting by $D+R\mapsto G(D+R)G^{-1}$.

Here identity modulo $I$ can equivalently be stated as $(G-\operatorname{id})(C_B)\subseteq F^1C_B$. To see the filtration implication without assuming that $I$ is finitely generated, observe that $F^qC_B$ is the closure of $C\otimes I^q$: modulo $F^n$, $n>q$, every element lifts from $C\otimes I^q$. By $B$-linearity a continuous map with image in $F^1$ carries that dense submodule into $F^{q+1}$; closedness gives the same inclusion on all $F^q$.

This contract uses all continuous coefficient-complete Taylor operations. It does not identify them with a naive algebraic tensor $\operatorname{Hom}_k(W,U)\otimes I$ when the coefficient algebra is infinite dimensional. Over a finite-dimensional coefficient algebra, expanding in a finite coefficient basis does give the usual tensor identification, without any finite-dimensionality assumption on $W,U$.

Use [[def-coefficient-complete-codifferential-deformation]]. The order filtration on $E$ is separated and complete, with $F^pE\,F^qE\subseteq F^{p+q}E$. The coderivations form a closed graded Lie subalgebra for

$$[P,Q]=PQ-(-1)^{|P||Q|}QP.$$

With $dT=[D,T]$, the positive-order space $\mathfrak g=F^1\mathfrak l$ is a complete filtered differential graded Lie algebra, with $F^p\mathfrak g=F^p\mathfrak l$ for $p\ge1$, $d(F^p\mathfrak g)\subseteq F^p\mathfrak g$, and $[F^p\mathfrak g,F^q\mathfrak g]\subseteq F^{p+q}\mathfrak g$.

Let $E$ be any unital associative $k$-algebra over a characteristic-zero field, with descending two-sided filtration $F^0E=E$, $F^pE\,F^qE\subseteq F^{p+q}E$, and $E\cong\varprojlim E/F^nE$. Commutativity is not assumed. The formulas

$$\exp X=\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{X^j}{j!},\qquad \log(1+N)=\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{(-1)^{j-1}N^j}{j}$$

give mutually inverse bijections $F^1E\leftrightarrow1+F^1E$, and $\exp(-X)$ is the inverse of $\exp X$. For $X\in F^1E$ and $T\in E$,

$$\exp(X)T\exp(-X)=\sum_{r\ge0}\frac{(\operatorname{ad}_X)^r(T)}{r!},\qquad \operatorname{ad}_X(T)=XT-TX.$$

The same conclusions apply to degree-zero $X$ in a graded algebra; $T$ may have any homogeneous degree. In particular they apply to the complete endomorphism algebra in [[def-coefficient-complete-codifferential-deformation]] once its completeness is established.

For the coefficient-complete tensor or symmetric carrier in [[def-coefficient-complete-codifferential-deformation]], exponential and logarithm restrict to mutually inverse bijections

$$F^1\mathfrak l^0\ \longleftrightarrow\ \{G:\ G\text{ is an allowed identity-modulo-}I\text{ coalgebra automorphism}\}.$$

In particular the logarithm of every such automorphism is a continuous counital coaugmentation-preserving coderivation; no finite-dimensionality or algebraic nilpotence of $I$ is required.

Let $\mathfrak g$ be a cohomologically graded Lie algebra over a characteristic-zero field: its degree-zero bracket is graded skew, satisfies graded Jacobi, and a degree-one map $d$ satisfies $d^2=0$ and $d[x,y]=[dx,y]+(-1)^{|x|}[x,dy]$. Suppose its separated complete positive filtration is preserved by $d$ and satisfies $[F^r\mathfrak g,F^s\mathfrak g]\subseteq F^{r+s}\mathfrak g$. With $s:\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak g[1]$ of degree $-1$, set

$$q_1(sx)=-s(dx),\qquad q_2(sx,sy)=(-1)^{|x|}s[x,y],\qquad q_n=0\ (n\ge3).$$

These operations define a complete filtered shifted L∞-algebra. Its degree-zero Maurer–Cartan elements are exactly $sR$, where $R\in F^1\mathfrak g^1$ satisfies $dR+[R,R]/2=0$. Its elementary gauge paths are exactly $R'=-d\xi+[\xi,R]$ with $\xi\in F^1\mathfrak g^0[t]^{\wedge}$, under $w=sR$, $a=s\xi$.

Let $W$ be a complete filtered shifted L∞-algebra over a characteristic-zero field $k$. Put $P=F^1W$ with its induced filtration. This is a complete closed subspace: it is the kernel of $W\to W/F^1W$, and compatible cosets in $P/F^pW$ have their unique $W$-limit in that kernel. All $q_n$ preserve $P$.

The **completed polynomial coefficients** and **completed polynomial differential forms** mean

$$P[t]^{\wedge}=\varprojlim_p (P/F^pW)\otimes_k k[t],\qquad P\widehat\otimes\Omega=\varprojlim_p (P/F^pW)\otimes_k k[t,dt],\quad |t|=0,\quad |dt|=1.$$

These are compatible polynomials in each quotient; their degrees need not have a common bound. Evaluation at $0,1$, differentiation, and integration from $0$ to $t$ are defined in every quotient by polynomial formulas and commute with reduction; integration uses $\int_0^t u^jdu=t^{j+1}/(j+1)$. Operations on these spaces are extended continuously, with each coefficient of a fixed quotient a finite sum.

Write $C(w)=\sum_{n\ge1}q_n(w^n)/n!$ and $q_1^w(a)=\sum_{n\ge0}q_{n+1}(w^n,a)/n!$. An **elementary gauge path** is a pair $w\in P^0[t]^{\wedge}$, $a\in P^{-1}[t]^{\wedge}$ such that $C(w)=0$ and $w'=q_1^w(a)$. Its endpoints are $w(0),w(1)$. **Gauge equivalence** is the equivalence relation generated by endpoints of these paths. A constant path has $a=0$; reversal is $(w(1-t),-a(1-t))$; finite chains give transitivity. Polynomial concatenation is not required.

For the polynomial-form interpretation, forms are placed on the right. For homogeneous $x_i\in P$, $\alpha_i\in\Omega$, the extension of $q_n$ has scalar sign $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}|\alpha_i||x_j|}$; its unary part also contains $(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes d\alpha$. The degree-zero form $z=w-a\,dt$ then satisfies $C_{\Omega}(z)=C(w)+(w'-q_1^w(a))dt$. Thus these paths are precisely Maurer–Cartan elements over the completed polynomial interval. This fixes a gauge construction using the full operations, rather than choosing an arbitrary equivalence relation on a solution set.

Let $A$ be a graded vector space over a field and let $m_n:A^{\otimes n}\to A$ have degree $2-n$, $n\ge1$. Use the Koszul tensor-map convention of [[def-koszul-sign-rule-for-graded-tensors]]. Write $X=A[1]$, $X^j=A^{j+1}$, and let $s_A:A\to X$ have degree $-1$ with inverse $u_A$ of degree $+1$. Put $c_n=n(n-1)/2$ and define

$$b_n=(-1)^{c_n}s_A m_n u_A^{\otimes n}:X^{\otimes n}\longrightarrow X.$$

Equivalently $b_n s_A^{\otimes n}=s_A m_n$ and $m_n=u_A b_n s_A^{\otimes n}$. Each $b_n$ has degree one. On homogeneous elements this formula reads

$$b_n(s_Aa_1,\ldots,s_Aa_n)=(-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^n(n-j)|a_j|}s_A m_n(a_1,\ldots,a_n).$$

Define the reduced tensor coalgebra $T^c(X)=\bigoplus_{n\ge1}X^{\otimes n}$ with reduced deconcatenation, and its coaugmented version $T^c_+(X)=k\cdot1\oplus T^c(X)$ with

$$\Delta(x_1\cdots x_N)=\sum_{i=0}^N(x_1\cdots x_i)\otimes(x_{i+1}\cdots x_N).$$

Empty words mean $1$. The $b_n$ extend uniquely to a degree-one coderivation $B:T^c_+(X)\to T^c_+(X)$ with $B(1)=0$, zero counit and corestrictions $b_n$. Explicitly

$$B|_{X^{\otimes N}}=\sum_{r+s+t=N\atop r,t\ge0,\ s\ge1}1^{\otimes r}\otimes b_s\otimes1^{\otimes t}.$$

Then $B^2=0$ if and only if the $m_n$ satisfy precisely the unsuspended A∞ identities of [[def-a-infinity-algebra]], with sign $(-1)^{r+st}$ in every arity. This gives a bijection between those uncurved structures and such square-zero coderivations. The same correspondence holds after removing the coaugmentation summand. No arity-zero operation or tensor completion is included.

Moreover, for structures on $A,D$ and homogeneous maps $f_n:A^{\otimes n}\to D$ of degree $1-n$, define degree-zero maps

$$F_n=(-1)^{c_n}s_D f_n u_A^{\otimes n}.$$

They extend uniquely to a coaugmentation- and counit-preserving coalgebra map $F:T^c_+(A[1])\to T^c_+(D[1])$, and $FB_A=B_DF$ if and only if $f$ satisfies exactly [[def-a-infinity-morphism]], including its right-hand sign

$$\eta(i_1,\ldots,i_q)=\sum_{j=1}^{q-1}(q-j)(i_j-1).$$

Composition of these coalgebra maps corresponds to the unsuspended Taylor composition $h_N=\sum_{q,\ i_1+\cdots+i_q=N}(-1)^\eta g_q(f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_q})$. In particular the correspondence respects identities.

The fixed signs give $b_1=s_A m_1u_A$ and $b_2=-s_A m_2(u_A\otimes u_A)$. The latter is an equality of graded maps: evaluated on $s_Aa\otimes s_Ab$ it is $(-1)^{|a|}s_A m_2(a,b)$. Replacing every $b_n$ simultaneously by $-b_n$ preserves both the square-zero condition and the morphism equation when done on both algebras; changing just one arity is not part of this correspondence.

Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field ([[def-field]],
[[def-ring-characteristic]]), and let $V=\bigoplus_{j\in\mathbb Z}V^j$ be a
graded $k$-vector space. Use the cohomological suspension

$$W=V[1],\qquad W^j=V^{j+1}.$$

The reduced cofree conilpotent cocommutative coalgebra on $W$ is the
$S^c(W)=\bigoplus_{n\ge1}S^n(W)$ of
[[def-reduced-graded-symmetric-coalgebra]], with its cofree property proved
in [[lem-reduced-graded-symmetric-coalgebra-is-cofree]].

An **L∞-algebra on $V$ in the shifted coalgebra convention** is a degree $+1$
coderivation $Q:S^c(W)\to S^c(W)$ with $Q^2=0$ and no arity-zero component.
A coderivation satisfies
$\bar\Delta Q=(Q\otimes1+1\otimes Q)\bar\Delta$, with the Koszul sign on
$1\otimes Q$, as defined in
[[lem-coderivation-extension-from-corestrictions]]. Its corestrictions are

$$q_n=\pi_1 Q|_{S^n(W)}:S^n(W)\longrightarrow W,\qquad |q_n|=+1 \quad(n\ge1),$$

where $\pi_1:S^c(W)\to S^1(W)=W$ is the length-one projection. Conversely,
each such family determines a unique coderivation by that lemma. The
condition $Q^2=0$ is equivalent to the higher Jacobi identities proved in
[[lem-square-zero-coderivation-is-higher-jacobi-identities]].

This is the shifted convention only: no unsuspended skew operations $l_n$ or
translation formula for them is asserted. Curved $L_\infty$ structures with
an arity-zero term are outside this definition.

boundaries.evidence: Definition and Statement: zero carrier is allowed; no positive-arity operation is evaluated on an empty list. Coaugmentation and zero-nullary conditions are explicit.

Definition and Statement: all-zero operations and zero positive filtration are permitted. The displayed formulas remain valid on zero inputs; the zero parameter, when present, yields the constant path.
Definition and Statement: the coaugmented coalgebra has scalar identity; maps preserve coaugmentation and coderivations kill it. The local proof retains the scalar component explicitly.

Definition and Statement: finite nilpotent quotients are included, and complete objects are separated inverse limits. Every infinite expression is justified by finite stabilization modulo the specified filtration.

Definition and Statement: elementary gauge paths have evaluations at zero and one. The local proof fixes the initial value, preserves endpoint evaluation under morphisms, or constructs the explicit path joining equivalent objects, as applicable.
Definition and Statement: all series, partitions, interpolation and Picard limits are explicitly prescribed. Uniqueness in each separated inverse limit avoids an unspecified choice of solution.
Statement and proof: each asserted identification is proved in its forward direction by curvature, square-zero expansion, or actual conjugation of the given object.

Statement and proof: reverse identifications use subtraction of the base codifferential, logarithms of every allowed automorphism, or explicit gauge paths, retaining the full specified equivalence group.

thm-maurer-cartan-elements-classify-fixe.finite_check_disposition: No executable finite-smoke assertion is claimed. Finite arity, unit-position and quotient-stabilization cases are proved symbolically in the actual numbered proof; infinite completion follows by compatible separated quotients.

derivations.claim: Put $V_B=\varprojlim_n(A[1]\otimes_k B/I^n)$ and $V_B^{\widehat\otimes r}=\varprojlim_n((A[1])^{\otimes r}\otimes_k B/I^n)$. A continuous homogeneous positive-arity Taylor map $f:V_B^{\widehat\otimes r}\to V_B$ of degree $u$ extends by inserting $f$ in every consecutive block of a word, with sign $(-1)^{u(|v_1|+\cdots+|v_{i-1}|)}$ for a block starting at $i$. Each word has only finitely many such blocks. Splitting the output word shows the coderivation equation: the replaced block lies entirely on one side of a coproduct split, and its insertion sign agrees with that side's graded tensor action. Thus these formulas define the coderivation and extend continuously through coefficient completion. Conversely, applying the iterated reduced coproduct and projecting every factor to length one expresses the length-$j$ component of a coderivation as the sum with its length-one projection on one of the $j$ input factors. Its other components are the untouched factors. This follows by iterating the coderivation equation. It determines every length component uniquely, and proves there is no output of length greater than the input length because all $j$ factors must be nonempty. The argument holds at each coefficient quotient and then in the limit. Thus these Taylor maps give every coaugmented counital coderivation uniquely.

For clarity first allow graded $A$ and a degree-zero product. With $|sa|=|a|-1$, the binary map $b_\mu(sa,sb)=(-1)^{|a|}s\mu(a,b)$ has degree one and equals $-s\mu(s^{-1}\otimes s^{-1})$, since the tensor-map sign on $(sa,sb)$ is $(-1)^{|a|-1}$. Its insertion extension from step 1.1 is therefore precisely fixed, including signs. Its square is a coderivation because $b_\mu^2=[b_\mu,b_\mu]/2$ and coderivations are closed under graded commutators by [[lem-complete-coderivations-form-a-filtered-differential-graded-lie-algebra]]. Its only possibly nonzero Taylor projection has arity three and is $(-1)^{|b|}s(\mu(\mu(a,b),c)-\mu(a,\mu(b,c)))$. Indeed the first association has sign $(-1)^{|a|+|a|+|b|}$, and the second has sign $(-1)^{|a|-1+|b|+|a|}$. Thus its square is zero exactly when the product is associative.

Return to degree-zero $A$, so $A[1]$ has degree $-1$ and the displayed binary sign is $+1$. A Taylor map of degree $u$ from arity $r$ to length one can be nonzero only when $-r+u=-1$, namely $u=r-1$. Thus every degree-one coderivation is binary and every degree-zero coderivation is unary. Step 2.1 proves that $D=b_\mu$ is square-zero, and the same computation proves that a degree-one $R=b_\alpha$ satisfies $(D+R)^2=0$ exactly when $\mu+\alpha$ is associative. A continuous bilinear map is understood on $M\widehat\otimes_B M=\varprojlim_n(A^{\otimes2}\otimes_k B/I^n)$; the condition $R\in F^1$ says its coefficient image lies in $F^1M$. No naive algebraic tensor of a Hom space with $I$ is used.

For an ordinary $r$-cochain $f$, denote the Taylor coderivation with projection $q_f(sa_1\otimes\cdots\otimes sa_r)=sf(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ by $q_f$; it has degree $r-1$. Call $f$ normalized when any argument $e$ makes it zero. A Taylor insertion contributing to $q_fq_g$ has the form $f(a_1,\ldots,g(a_i,\ldots,a_{i+t-1}),\ldots,a_{r+t-1})$, up to its specified sign. If a unit argument lies inside the inserted block, $g$ vanishes; if outside, a remaining argument of $f$ is the unit and $f$ vanishes. Thus every insertion of normalized cochains is normalized separately, and so are their commutators. Evaluation with any input fixed to $e$ is a closed continuous condition. Hence $\mathfrak n$ is a closed graded Lie subalgebra with the inherited additive filtration bound.

A degree-zero coalgebra map $G$ on this carrier is determined by its length-one projection, and that projection can be nonzero only on arity one, since all inputs of arity $r$ have degree $-r$ and $B$ has degree zero. To justify the determination explicitly, apply the iterated coproduct of $G$ and project its $j$ outputs to length one; the resulting length-$j$ component is the $j$-fold tensor of the length-one projection applied to the iterated coproduct of the input. Coaugmentation and counit fix the length-zero part. Hence $G=T^c(g)$ for the unary map $g:M\to M$; it is an allowed automorphism exactly when $g$ is continuous, invertible, and congruent to the identity modulo $I$. Conversely that tensor extension is a coalgebra automorphism by deconcatenation, with inverse $T^c(g^{-1})$.

Although $b_\mu$ is not normalized, its commutator preserves normalization. Write the usual Hochschild differential as $(\delta_\mu f)(a_1,\ldots,a_{r+1})=a_1f(a_2,\ldots,a_{r+1})+\sum_{i=1}^r(-1)^if(a_1,\ldots,a_ia_{i+1},\ldots,a_{r+1})+(-1)^{r+1}f(a_1,\ldots,a_r)a_{r+1}$. The insertion convention gives exactly $\pi_1[b_\mu,q_f](sa_1,\ldots,sa_{r+1})=(-1)^{r-1}s(\delta_\mu f)(a_1,\ldots,a_{r+1})$. Indeed the left outer product has coefficient $(-1)^{r-1}$, from moving $q_f$ past $sa_1$; the right outer product has coefficient $+1$; and the $i$-th adjacent multiplication term in $-(-1)^{r-1}q_fb_\mu$ has coefficient $(-1)^{r+i-1}$. These are exactly the asserted common sign times the Hochschild coefficients.

A degree-zero $X\in F^1\mathfrak n$ is $q_\xi$ for a continuous unary $\xi$ with $\xi(e)=0$. Since $\xi^j(e)=0$ for all $j\ge1$, $g=\exp\xi$ fixes $e$. Conversely if $g\equiv\operatorname{id}\pmod I$ fixes $e$, then $(g-\operatorname{id})(e)=0$ and every positive power does too, so $\log(g)(e)=0$. Both series converge by [[lem-noncommutative-filtered-exponential-and-logarithm]], applied to the unary complete endomorphism algebra or to length one in $C_B$. Also $\exp(q_\xi)=T^c(\exp\xi)$: the left side is a coalgebra map by [[thm-coalgebra-automorphism-logarithms-are-coderivations]], has unary projection $\exp\xi$, and is determined by that projection by step 4.2. Applying the inverse logarithm proves $\log(T^c(g))=q_{\log(g)}$. Consequently exponentials of $F^1\mathfrak n^0$ give exactly all the required unit-preserving changes of variables, including the reverse implication that $\exp\xi(e)=e$ forces $\xi(e)=0$.

If the unit occurs at an interior position $2\le j\le r$, the adjacent multiplication terms $i=j-1$ and $i=j$ in $\delta_\mu f$ have identical remaining arguments and opposite signs; every other term retains the unit inside $f$ and vanishes. If $j=1$, the first outer product term cancels the $i=1$ multiplication term, using $ef=f$. If $j=r+1$, the $i=r$ multiplication term cancels the last outer product term, using $fe=f$. In both endpoint cases all remaining terms vanish by normalization. These arguments also include $r=1$, where only the endpoint cases occur. Thus $\delta_\mu$ preserves normalization and $[D,\mathfrak n]\subseteq\mathfrak n$. Closedness in step 4.1 and [[lem-complete-coderivations-form-a-filtered-differential-graded-lie-algebra]] now give a complete filtered differential graded Lie algebra $F^1\mathfrak n$.

By the direct identity $(D+R)^2=[D,R]+[R,R]/2$ and the preceding binary degree and associativity computations, its Maurer–Cartan elements are exactly associative products $\mu+\alpha$ with the specified reduction and with $\alpha$ normalized. Since $\mu(e,a)=a=\mu(a,e)$, normalization is equivalent to $(\mu+\alpha)(e,a)=a=(\mu+\alpha)(a,e)$. Conversely any continuous fixed-unit product with this reduction has such a normalized difference $\alpha$. Hence the claimed object correspondence holds in both directions. In particular at arity two the differential sign is $\pi_1[D,b_\alpha]=-s\delta_\mu\alpha$, while $\pi_1[b_\alpha,b_\alpha]/2=s(\alpha(\alpha(a,b),c)-\alpha(a,\alpha(b,c)))$, so its suspended Maurer–Cartan equation is exactly the expanded associator, with no implicit sign convention.

On binary Taylor projections, conjugation by $G=T^c(g)$ gives $b_{m'}$ with $m'(a,b)=g(m(g^{-1}a,g^{-1}b))$. If $m$ has unit $e$ and $g(e)=e$, then $m'(e,a)=a=m'(a,e)$; reduction modulo $I$ remains $\mu$. Thus the full subgroup just identified acts on exactly the fixed-unit products in step 7.1, by the stated ordinary transport formula.

The gauge and conjugation proof in [[thm-maurer-cartan-elements-classify-fixed-carrier-codifferential-deformations]] restricts to this normalized subalgebra. In detail its variable unary parameter $\xi(t)$ satisfies $\xi(t)e=0$, and its solution $g'=\xi(t)g$, $g(0)=\operatorname{id}$ has $(g(e)-e)'=\xi(t)(g(e)-e)$ with zero initial value. The same coefficient-order integral induction proves $g(e)=e$. Hence every normalized gauge path has an actual unit-preserving endpoint automorphism. Conversely any allowed unit-preserving $g$ has normalized $\log(g)$ by step 5.2, and $\exp(t\log(g))$ fixes $e$ and gives a normalized gauge path. Therefore normalized gauge equivalence is precisely the entire fixed-unit change-of-variables equivalence, rather than merely the unrestricted codifferential equivalence.

Finally for $B=k[\![h]\!]$, a continuous coefficient-complete bilinear map is uniquely its sequence of coefficient maps $B_j:A\otimes A\to A$: apply it to constant inputs and expand each output in $A[\![h]\!]$, then use $k[\![h]\!]$-linearity and continuity. Every sequence conversely defines such a map because only finitely many coefficients contribute modulo $h^n$. Reduction fixes the zero coefficient to $\mu$, and normalization is coefficientwise $B_j(e,a)=B_j(a,e)=0$. Thus step 7.1's object bijection and step 9.1's full equivalence correspondence apply to the formal products in the statement, including the initial commutative-algebra case.

Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, let $B$ be a commutative unital $k$-algebra concentrated in degree zero, and let $I$ be an ideal such that $B\cong\varprojlim_{n\ge1}B/I^n$. Nilpotent ideals are included. Let $V$ be any graded $k$-vector space; no finite-dimensionality assumption is made. Use the graded tensor convention of [[def-koszul-sign-rule-for-graded-tensors]].

The carrier $C$ is either the coaugmented tensor coalgebra $T^c(V)=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}V^{\otimes r}$ with deconcatenation, or the coaugmented graded symmetric coalgebra $S^c(V)=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}S^r(V)$ with unshuffle coproduct. For the latter, $S^r$ means graded symmetric coinvariants, and the coproduct sums over all divisions of the inputs into two ordered sublists, with the Koszul sign. The empty word is $1_C$, the counit $\epsilon$ is projection to length zero, and the coaugmentation is inclusion of scalars. These formulas specify the carrier without requiring a cofree universal property.

Define its coefficient completion, filtration, and tensor target by

$$C_B=\varprojlim_n(C\otimes_k B/I^n),\qquad F^nC_B=\ker(C_B\longrightarrow C\otimes_k B/I^n),\qquad F^0C_B=C_B.$$

$$C_B\widehat\otimes_B C_B=\varprojlim_n((C\otimes_k C)\otimes_k B/I^n).$$

All structure maps are extended through these inverse limits. This is coefficient completion of a direct sum: modulo each $I^n$ every element has finite length support. No unrestricted product over arities is included. Completed tensor powers and polynomial coefficients mean the analogous explicit inverse limits. A homogeneous map is understood in the grading induced by $C$, and continuity always means the displayed coefficient topology.

Let $E$ be the graded composition algebra of continuous $B$-linear filtration-preserving endomorphisms of $C_B$. Its order filtration is

$$F^pE=\{T:T(F^qC_B)\subseteq F^{p+q}C_B\text{ for every }q\ge0\}\quad(p\ge0).$$

Let $\mathfrak l\subset E$ be the homogeneous coderivations satisfying $T(1_C)=0$, $\epsilon T=0$, and

$$\Delta T=(T\otimes1+1\otimes T)\Delta.$$

The sign in $1\otimes T$ is the graded tensor sign. In particular these coderivations have zero nullary component. Fix $D\in\mathfrak l^1$ with $D^2=0$. A **coefficient-complete fixed-carrier codifferential deformation** is $D+R$ with $R\in F^1\mathfrak l^1$ and $(D+R)^2=0$. Its allowed equivalences are degree-zero continuous $B$-linear counital coaugmented coalgebra automorphisms $G$ such that $G-\operatorname{id}\in F^1E$, acting by $D+R\mapsto G(D+R)G^{-1}$.

Here identity modulo $I$ can equivalently be stated as $(G-\operatorname{id})(C_B)\subseteq F^1C_B$. To see the filtration implication without assuming that $I$ is finitely generated, observe that $F^qC_B$ is the closure of $C\otimes I^q$: modulo $F^n$, $n>q$, every element lifts from $C\otimes I^q$. By $B$-linearity a continuous map with image in $F^1$ carries that dense submodule into $F^{q+1}$; closedness gives the same inclusion on all $F^q$.

This contract uses all continuous coefficient-complete Taylor operations. It does not identify them with a naive algebraic tensor $\operatorname{Hom}_k(W,U)\otimes I$ when the coefficient algebra is infinite dimensional. Over a finite-dimensional coefficient algebra, expanding in a finite coefficient basis does give the usual tensor identification, without any finite-dimensionality assumption on $W,U$.

Use [[def-coefficient-complete-codifferential-deformation]]. The order filtration on $E$ is separated and complete, with $F^pE\,F^qE\subseteq F^{p+q}E$. The coderivations form a closed graded Lie subalgebra for

$$[P,Q]=PQ-(-1)^{|P||Q|}QP.$$

With $dT=[D,T]$, the positive-order space $\mathfrak g=F^1\mathfrak l$ is a complete filtered differential graded Lie algebra, with $F^p\mathfrak g=F^p\mathfrak l$ for $p\ge1$, $d(F^p\mathfrak g)\subseteq F^p\mathfrak g$, and $[F^p\mathfrak g,F^q\mathfrak g]\subseteq F^{p+q}\mathfrak g$.

Let $E$ be any unital associative $k$-algebra over a characteristic-zero field, with descending two-sided filtration $F^0E=E$, $F^pE\,F^qE\subseteq F^{p+q}E$, and $E\cong\varprojlim E/F^nE$. Commutativity is not assumed. The formulas

$$\exp X=\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{X^j}{j!},\qquad \log(1+N)=\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{(-1)^{j-1}N^j}{j}$$

give mutually inverse bijections $F^1E\leftrightarrow1+F^1E$, and $\exp(-X)$ is the inverse of $\exp X$. For $X\in F^1E$ and $T\in E$,

$$\exp(X)T\exp(-X)=\sum_{r\ge0}\frac{(\operatorname{ad}_X)^r(T)}{r!},\qquad \operatorname{ad}_X(T)=XT-TX.$$

The same conclusions apply to degree-zero $X$ in a graded algebra; $T$ may have any homogeneous degree. In particular they apply to the complete endomorphism algebra in [[def-coefficient-complete-codifferential-deformation]] once its completeness is established.

For the coefficient-complete tensor or symmetric carrier in [[def-coefficient-complete-codifferential-deformation]], exponential and logarithm restrict to mutually inverse bijections

$$F^1\mathfrak l^0\ \longleftrightarrow\ \{G:\ G\text{ is an allowed identity-modulo-}I\text{ coalgebra automorphism}\}.$$

In particular the logarithm of every such automorphism is a continuous counital coaugmentation-preserving coderivation; no finite-dimensionality or algebraic nilpotence of $I$ is required.

Use [[def-coefficient-complete-codifferential-deformation]], and put $\mathfrak g=F^1\mathfrak l$, $d=[D,-]$. Then

$$R\longmapsto D+R$$

is a bijection between $\{R\in\mathfrak g^1:dR+[R,R]/2=0\}$ and all the stated fixed-carrier codifferential deformations. It identifies their equivalence classes by all allowed coalgebra automorphisms with Maurer–Cartan gauge classes of the shifted filtered L∞-algebra of [[lem-filtered-graded-lie-algebra-defines-a-shifted-l-infinity-algebra]], using [[def-filtered-maurer-cartan-gauge-path]].

More explicitly, the full allowed group is $\exp(\mathfrak g^0)$, with group operation inherited from composition, and its action on Maurer–Cartan elements is

$$R\longmapsto e^{\operatorname{ad}_X}R-\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{(\operatorname{ad}_X)^j(dX)}{(j+1)!},\qquad X\in\mathfrak g^0.$$

The gauge-path relation, including variable parameters, equals the orbit relation of this action. No assertion that an unspecified deformation problem is governed by an arbitrary L∞-algebra is included.

For the tensor carrier on $A[1]$, this is the fixed-carrier A∞-structure correspondence in the native unsuspended convention, using [[lem-unsuspended-a-infinity-identities-are-tensor-codifferentials]], including its morphism signs. For the symmetric carrier on $V[1]$, it is the fixed-carrier L∞ correspondence in [[def-shifted-coalgebra-l-infinity-algebra]]. Both identifications are coefficient-complete and retain every allowed identity-modulo-ideal equivalence.

Let $A$ be a commutative unital algebra over $\mathbb R$, with
multiplication $m(f,g)=fg$. Write $A\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$ for the real formal
power-series module with coefficients in $A$; its underlying coefficient
and Cauchy-product conventions are those of
[[def-formal-power-series-and-coefficient-extraction]]. The $\hbar$-adic
topology is the coefficient-prefix topology of
[[def-formal-order-and-x-adic-topology]]: two series are close modulo
$\hbar^N$ when their coefficients agree in degrees below $N$.

A **formal associative deformation** of $A$ is specified by real-bilinear
maps $B_r:A\times A\to A$ for $r\geq 1$, with $B_0:=m$, and the
product
$$\left(\sum_{i\geq0}\hbar^if_i\right)\star \left(\sum_{j\geq0}\hbar^jg_j\right) =\sum_{N\geq0}\hbar^N\sum_{\substack{i,j,r\geq0\\i+j+r=N}}B_r(f_i,g_j).$$
For each fixed $N$ the inner sum is finite, so this formula defines a
coefficientwise-continuous, $\mathbb R\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$-bilinear product. It is
required to be associative and unital with unit $1$; equivalently,
$B_r(1,f)=B_r(f,1)=0$ for $r\geq1$. Reduction modulo $\hbar$ is the
original product $m$.

This definition alone asserts no differential-order condition, no specified
first-order bracket, no convergence at a numerical value of $\hbar$, and no
existence or classification theorem.

derivations.claim: The only nonzero shifted identity is $q_1^2=0$, which is the complex axiom. Its unary operation preserves the two-step filtration, and higher operations vanish, so all additive filtration inclusions hold. The filtration is separated and complete since the quotient by $F^2$ is $P$ itself. Its curvature is $C(w)=q_1w$, so the Maurer–Cartan set is $\ker q_1$ in degree zero.

Here $q_1^w=q_1$ independently of $w$. Any path therefore satisfies $w(1)-w(0)=q_1(\int_0^1a(t)dt)$, so its endpoints have the same cohomology class. A finite chain has that property as well. Conversely, if $w_1-w_0=q_1b$ with $b\in P^{-1}$, take $a(t)=b$ and $w(t)=w_0+tq_1b$. This satisfies the path equation and has $q_1w(t)=0$ since $q_1^2=0$; it is also the unique flow in [F2]. Thus the gauge equivalence classes are precisely the stated cohomology classes.

In both concrete complexes $q_1$ is zero on degree zero, so the curvature equation is identically zero on $ke$. In the zero complex the image from degree minus one is zero, giving quotient $ke$. In the second complex that image is all $ke$, giving a single class. The two quotient computations follow from step 2.1 with identical degree-zero solution loci.

Let $W$ be a complete filtered shifted L∞-algebra over a characteristic-zero field $k$. Put $P=F^1W$ with its induced filtration. This is a complete closed subspace: it is the kernel of $W\to W/F^1W$, and compatible cosets in $P/F^pW$ have their unique $W$-limit in that kernel. All $q_n$ preserve $P$.

The **completed polynomial coefficients** and **completed polynomial differential forms** mean

$$P[t]^{\wedge}=\varprojlim_p (P/F^pW)\otimes_k k[t],\qquad P\widehat\otimes\Omega=\varprojlim_p (P/F^pW)\otimes_k k[t,dt],\quad |t|=0,\quad |dt|=1.$$

These are compatible polynomials in each quotient; their degrees need not have a common bound. Evaluation at $0,1$, differentiation, and integration from $0$ to $t$ are defined in every quotient by polynomial formulas and commute with reduction; integration uses $\int_0^t u^jdu=t^{j+1}/(j+1)$. Operations on these spaces are extended continuously, with each coefficient of a fixed quotient a finite sum.

Write $C(w)=\sum_{n\ge1}q_n(w^n)/n!$ and $q_1^w(a)=\sum_{n\ge0}q_{n+1}(w^n,a)/n!$. An **elementary gauge path** is a pair $w\in P^0[t]^{\wedge}$, $a\in P^{-1}[t]^{\wedge}$ such that $C(w)=0$ and $w'=q_1^w(a)$. Its endpoints are $w(0),w(1)$. **Gauge equivalence** is the equivalence relation generated by endpoints of these paths. A constant path has $a=0$; reversal is $(w(1-t),-a(1-t))$; finite chains give transitivity. Polynomial concatenation is not required.

For the polynomial-form interpretation, forms are placed on the right. For homogeneous $x_i\in P$, $\alpha_i\in\Omega$, the extension of $q_n$ has scalar sign $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}|\alpha_i||x_j|}$; its unary part also contains $(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes d\alpha$. The degree-zero form $z=w-a\,dt$ then satisfies $C_{\Omega}(z)=C(w)+(w'-q_1^w(a))dt$. Thus these paths are precisely Maurer–Cartan elements over the completed polynomial interval. This fixes a gauge construction using the full operations, rather than choosing an arbitrary equivalence relation on a solution set.

In the setting of [[def-filtered-maurer-cartan-gauge-path]], for every $w_*\in\operatorname{MC}(P)$ and every $a\in P^{-1}[t]^{\wedge}$ there is a unique $w\in P^0[t]^{\wedge}$ with $w(0)=w_*$ and $w'=q_1^w(a)$. It satisfies $C(w)=0$, so it is an elementary gauge path. Modulo every $F^pW$ the construction stabilizes after finitely many polynomial Picard iterations; no globally bounded polynomial degree is asserted.
